title: Flat restriction of scalars preserves K-injectives
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings such that for every
scheme $X$ the extension of scalars $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$ preserves finite limits
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]). Then for every scheme $X$ the restriction of scalars
$\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\colon\Mod_{\Lambda'_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ sends K-injective complexes
([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]) to K-injective complexes.

proof.text:
Let $I$ be a K-injective complex of $\Lambda'_X$-modules and $C$ an acyclic complex of
$\Lambda_X$-modules. By the adjunction $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$
([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]), applied termwise and passed to the homotopy category,
$\Hom_K(C,\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}I)\cong\Hom_K(\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}C,I)$. The functor
$\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$ is exact (right exact as a left adjoint, left exact by assumption),
so $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}C$ is acyclic and the right side vanishes since $I$ is K-injective.
